definitions.gloss: to launch; to start up; to boot up
definitions.explanation: to initiate or establish something new, especially a business, project, or computer system

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{会社|かいしゃ}を{立|た}ち{上|あ}げた。
パソコンを{立|た}ち{上|あ}げるのに{時間|じかん}がかかる。
examples.english: It takes time to boot up the computer.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{起業家|きぎょうか}として{複数|ふくすう}のスタートアップを{立|た}ち{上|あ}げてきた。
examples.english: As an entrepreneur, she has launched multiple startups.

notes:
{立|た}ち{上|あ}げる is a compound verb combining {立|た}つ (to stand) + {上|あ}げる (to raise), expressing the idea of getting something up and running.

VERB TYPE:
- Ichidan verb (る-verb)
- Transitive

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {会社|かいしゃ}を{立|た}ち{上|あ}げる (to launch a company)
- {事業|じぎょう}を{立|た}ち{上|あ}げる (to start a business)
- プロジェクトを{立|た}ち{上|あ}げる (to launch a project)
- パソコン/システムを{立|た}ち{上|あ}げる (to boot up a computer/system)
- ウェブサイトを{立|た}ち{上|あ}げる (to launch a website)

USAGE NOTES:
- Often used in business and IT contexts
- The IT usage (boot up) comes from the physical metaphor of getting something standing and running
- Compare with {起動|きどう}する which is more technical for systems

RELATED TERMS:
- {立|た}ち{上|あ}がる (intransitive: to stand up, to start up)
- {起動|きどう}する (to start/boot - more technical)
- {創業|そうぎょう}する (to found - more formal)

REGISTER: Neutral. Common in business, IT, and everyday contexts.
